title: Staged regional GPU allocation and throttle schedule (2026 planning)
content:
Executive summary:

This working doc outlines a staged, region-aware GPU allocation plan and throttling schedule for 2026 focused on reducing cold-starts, keeping unit cost predictable, and prioritizing APAC growth while preserving NA/EU SLAs. It ties capacity hedges to concrete rollout windows, pre-warm triggers, and fallback policies so product teams can plan feature launches with clear risk profiles.

High-level goals:
- Ensure 99.5% availability for hosted inference in NA/EU; aim for 99.0% in initial APAC waves until regional telemetry stabilizes.
- Minimize token-level cost inflation by combining reserved capacity (Dedicated) with opportunistic on-demand burst and pre-warmed pools.
- Limit tail latency regressions during global events (major product launches, demos) with automated regional throttles and fallbacks.

Key assumptions (input data and constraints):
- Forecast workload growth: baseline token throughput +55% YoY for APAC, +28% YoY for NA, +22% YoY for EU (based on Q3 usage signals and sales pipeline).
- Preferred instance families: A100-80GB equivalent for high-throughput variants; T4/RTX6000 equivalents for cost-sensitive embedding workloads.
- Lead time for reserved capacity procurement: 8–12 weeks (cloud reservations + contract negotiation).
- Budget constraint: incremental quarterly cap of $600k for public cloud GPU spend (hosted + burst). Dedicated reserved commitments negotiated separately.

Regional staged capacity plan (quarter-level snapshots):
- NA (primary market):
  Q1 2026: baseline 320 vGPU-equivalents (mixed A100/T4), target utilization 58%
  Q2 2026: +48 vGPU -> 368 total, target utilization 60%
  Q3 2026: +24 vGPU -> 392 total, target utilization 62%
  Q4 2026: +40 vGPU -> 432 total, target utilization 64%

- EU (secondary, steady growth):
  Q1 2026: baseline 160 vGPU-equivalents, target utilization 55%
  Q2 2026: +20 -> 180, target utilization 57%
  Q3 2026: +20 -> 200, target utilization 58%
  Q4 2026: +30 -> 230, target utilization 60%

- APAC (priority expansion, phased rollout):
  Wave 0 (Jan-Feb 2026 - pilot): 24 vGPU pre-warm in Tokyo + 16 in Singapore (regional small pool for demos, latency-sensitive apps)
  Q1 2026 (Wave 1): 80 vGPU total across APAC regions, utilization target 35% (intentional headroom to absorb demand spikes)
  Q2 2026 (Wave 2): expand to 160 vGPU, utilization target 50%
  Q3 2026 (Wave 3): expand to 280 vGPU, utilization target 60%
  Q4 2026: stabilization and evaluate dedicated reservations once 30-day steady utilization >55%

Notes on capacity numbers: these are expressed in "vGPU-equivalents" to simplify heterogenous shapes. Final instance mapping will be decided by the kernel-selection planner (A100/RTX/T4 mixes).

Rollout timeline and gating criteria (APAC-first cadence):
- Precondition: monitoring + tracing filters instrumented for region-level p99/p50 latency, per-model token cost, and KV cache hit rate (Engineering ticket INFRA-3291).
- Wave 0 (pilot): Jan 05—Feb 15 2026. Goal: validate cold-start profile, cross-region replication, telemetry. Gating: p99 latency < 450ms for small seq lengths on 95% of requests; rollout hold if error rate > 1.5% sustained over 10m.
- Wave 1: Mar 01—Mar 31 2026. Additional scale + pre-warm hooks for product-runbooks. Gating: 7-day rolling average of successful falls back <0.5% and KV cache hit > 18%.
- Wave 2: May 01—Jun 15 2026. Add burst configurations and cross-zone fallback policy. Gating: cost-per-token delta vs baseline < 12% (acceptable), and latency SLOs maintained.
- Wave 3: Aug 01—Sep 30 2026. Prepare for dedicated reservation negotiations if utilization thresholds met.

Throttle schedule and automated fallback policies:
- Throttles operate at three levels: per-route soft throttle (graceful 429s; client-visible), regional capacity throttle (moves heavy requests to cheaper model variants), and emergency global throttle (critical protection; fallback to cached responses or read-only modes).
- Example throttle thresholds (configurable):
  - soft throttle: queue depth > 1200 requests OR average latency > 2x SLO for 60s
  - regional capacity throttle: regional GPU utilization > 88% for 5m AND queue growth positive for 2m
  - emergency global throttle: failure rate > 3% AND critical services impacted
- Fallback policy chain: preferred variant -> compatible smaller quantized variant -> cached prefix response -> 429 with Retry-After header.

Pre-warm and burst mechanics:
- Pre-warm windows scheduled to match predictable traffic increments (marketing campaigns, product launches). Pre-warm policy: allocate ephemeral pre-warm nodes 40–60m before expected surge, drain gracefully over 10–30m after surge.
- Idle pre-warm budget per region initially capped: NA 10% of baseline, EU 8%, APAC 12% (APAC slightly higher to offset network variability).
- Burst strategy: allow on-demand burst capacity up to 25% of regional baseline for short windows (<=4 hours) paid from a shared burst budget; track usage against quarterly cap.

Cost sensitivity scenarios (quick view):
- Conservative (lower cloud prices): mix 65% reserved + 35% on-demand; quarterly cloud spend for hosted GPU ~ $420k.
- Base (current market): 50% reserved + 50% on-demand; quarterly spend ~ $540k.
- Stress (spot market constrained): 30% reserved + 70% on-demand; quarterly spend ~ $720k (need to throttle growth or push to Dedicated).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: APAC network egress variability increases tail latency. Mitigation: higher APAC pre-warm, aggressive KV prefix caching, colocate smaller model variants near edge.
- Risk: procurement lead-time misses causing capacity gaps. Mitigation: short-term burst contracts with multiple cloud partners, keep 6–8 week hedged buffer.
- Risk: unexpected spike from an enterprise customer. Mitigation: dedicated backstop pool for enterprise customers with explicit SLAs and rate-limited failover.

Operational playbook snippets (for runbooks):
- If regional p95 latency increases > 35% for 10m: trigger automated scale + notify on-call infra + pause non-critical background jobs.
- If regional utilization > 92% for 5m: enable regional capacity throttle and start contingency burst (if budget available).
- During pre-warm: watch KV cache warm rate; if cache hit < target after 20m, escalate to model-owner to evaluate prompt-sharding.

Metrics to track (dashboard suggestions):
- Per-region: vGPU utilization (p50/p95), queue depth, cold-start rate, KV cache hit rate, cost-per-token, fallback rate.
- Cross-region: lift ratio (APAC/NA p95 latency), burst usage vs budget, reservations lead-time compliance.

Next steps / action items (owners and rough dates):
- Instrumentation: complete region-level SLI tags (Marija) by 2025-12-20.
- Pilot config: deploy Wave 0 template (Evan) by 2026-01-02.
- Cost-model update: finance + infra to run scenario analysis for Q1 budget vote (Asha) by 2025-12-18.
- Reservation negotiation: procurement to start APAC footprint quotes (Diego) by 2026-03-01.

Open questions for review:
- Should we centralize APAC pre-warm in a single cloud region (Tokyo) or distribute across Tokyo+Singapore for redundancy? Pros/cons noted in comments.
- What is the acceptable cost uplift threshold for product teams to auto-accept smaller quantized fallbacks? Proposal: 10% token-cost uplift.

Appendix (short):
- Definitions: vGPU-equivalent = normalized capacity unit (A100-80GB = 4 vGPU-eq, RTX6000 = 1 vGPU-eq — final mapping TBD).
- Quick links: monitoring dashboard template (CONFLUENCE-Infra-Capacity-2026), ticket INFRA-3291 for region scheduler MR.

This doc is intentionally prescriptive but still a working draft — please add model-specific constraints and product launch dates so we can adapt pre-warm windows.
